Definition: from the same as G5584; a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote:--stone, voice.
BiblicalUsage: Psephos is a pebble, a stone used as a counter or a ballot, a vote. Paul says that when the saints were put to death at Jerusalem, he gave his voice against them. And to the overcomer at Pergamos, Christ promises a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two stones tell my whole story: Paul's black pebble voted for death, and Christ's white stone promises life and a new name.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
